findings: Dirty staged/unstaged/untracked content survives file and whole-turn rollback; user Git metadata is unchanged.
Only an observed contiguous tool write chain with supported pre/post snapshots is eligible for automatic rollback.
Conflicts block preflight; runtime failures compensate conditionally and retain needs-recovery when an external edit prevents compensation.
limitations: Windows regular-file bytes only; ACLs, permissions, empty directories, case-only rename and other platforms are not verified.
File symlink creation returned EPERM on this host; actual file-symlink execution remains unverified. Directory junction and hardlink tests ran.
Same canonical workspace must use a single host-owned store/lock mapping; other stores and external processes do not obey that lock.
Path checks and double scans cannot eliminate the final OS write race or establish authorship when external writes are indistinguishable.
Multi-file rollback is not an OS transaction; crash recovery and durable fsync require production implementation.
Ignored/builtin-excluded/nested repositories, files above 5 MiB, symlinks/junctions/hardlinks and external command/network effects are not rollback promises.
Ignored files store metadata only; excluded-directory contents are not scanned. No sensitive fixture content is stored for these paths.
Staging rename requires same volume; stale locks, manual overrides, UI, block rollback and GC policy remain later work.
ENOSPC/EACCES/EIO and timing races use explicitly labelled local injection, not genuine disk exhaustion or ACL incidents.
